claims.text: SOLID is an acronym for five design principles: Single Responsibility (SRP), Open/Closed (OCP), Liskov Substitution (LSP), Interface Segregation (ISP) and Dependency Inversion (DIP).
claims.source_hint: glossary entry solid; standard definition in software design literature

claims.text: The Single Responsibility Principle states that a class should have only one reason to change.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry srp; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: PlaceOrderSplit has Place plus four private static methods: FirstProblemWith (input checks), TotalWithShippingVnd (total plus shipping fee), Save and Notify (each a Console.WriteLine).
The shipping fee threshold 2_000_000 is in TotalWithShippingVnd; a new input check (e.g. at most 20 lines) would go in FirstProblemWith; Save and Notify only print lines.
PlaceOrderSplit.cs is under 40 lines at stage-0 (38 lines).
Each of the four requests in the situation (20-line cap, 1,500,000 free-shipping threshold, real saving, SMS) changes a different method, and all four methods are in PlaceOrderSplit.cs.
Splitting into one class per reason to change (validator, pricer, order saver, notifier), with the check-price-save-notify sequence left in Place as its own single reason, is what SRP asks for.
claims.source_hint: outline items 2 and 4; follows from the SRP definition

claims.text: Asking who would request a change is a practical way to spot distinct reasons to change.

self_check.notes: Outline item 4 said 'repository', a term taught later (design.l1.the-repository-layer); outline changed to 'order saver' and the lesson uses that.
